questions_visited.why_selected: Mapped evidence for the maximum-height condition and no-time equation.
questions_visited.assessed_demand: Set vertical velocity to zero at the top, use vertical initial velocity, and calculate maximum height.
questions_visited.reasoning_route: Take upwards positive, set v=0 and a=-g, then solve v^2=u^2+2as.
questions_visited.misconception_or_distractor: Treating acceleration as zero at maximum height or using the full launch velocity instead of a vertical velocity.
lesson_sections_informed: The crucial instant at maximum height

questions_visited.why_selected: Mapped evidence showing time-to-top as an intermediate quantity in a longer route.
questions_visited.assessed_demand: Find time to maximum height then combine perpendicular displacements.
questions_visited.reasoning_route: Use v=u+at vertically to find the stage time, then apply later component processing.
questions_visited.misconception_or_distractor: Using the launch velocity after the maximum-height boundary or mixing component directions.

questions_visited.why_selected: Mapped evidence for upward and downward displacement signs around the zero-velocity instant.
questions_visited.assessed_demand: Find starting height from signed areas above and below a velocity-time graph.
questions_visited.reasoning_route: Split at v=0, calculate the upward and downward triangular displacements, then subtract to obtain starting height.
questions_visited.misconception_or_distractor: Adding areas as distances without signs or treating the maximum-height instant as zero acceleration.
